title: 第十五章 天阙第十六章 玄阴
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌

第二天上午，苏尘准时到了东街口那棵大槐树底下。
秋末的阳光比昨天暖和了些，照在青石板路上泛着一层淡淡的白光。街上的铺子已经开了大半，卖菜的、卖布的、卖早点的，吆喝声此起彼伏。空气里混着面饼的焦香和青菜上的露水味，是朔州城每个普通上午该有的样子。
苏尘在槐树底下站了不到片刻，就看见陆辞从街角走了过来。
他今天换了一身深灰色的窄袖便服，腰间还是挂着那块青玉佩，但少了几分昨日那种富家少爷的扎眼感，倒更像一个出门办事的少年。身后远远跟着那个灰衣护卫，这回保持了十几步的距离，没有再贴上来。
陆辞走到槐树底下，看了苏尘一眼，笑着打了个招呼：
“苏兄，早啊。“
“早。“
“吃了吗？“
“吃了。“
“我还没吃。“陆辞说得理所当然，像是完全不觉得让人等一个吃了早饭的自己有什么问题，“早上起晚了。陈叔催了我两回，我说跟人有约，他才没念叨——走吧，你先带我找个地方填填肚子。“
苏尘看了他一眼，转身往街里走。
陆辞跟上来，步子轻快，看起来心情不错。
苏尘带他去了东街拐角那家面摊——就是昨天提了一嘴的那家。
面摊不大，支着两口锅，一口煮面一口熬汤。老板是个五十来岁的大婶，围裙上沾着面粉，手劲儿大得很，面团在手里揉得虎虎生风。看见苏尘来了，点了点头算是打过招呼——这摊子苏尘偶尔会来，算不上熟客，但脸是认得的。
两个人找了张靠边的桌子坐下。陆辞要了一碗羊肉面，多加葱花，又要了两个烧饼。苏尘只要了一碗清汤，坐着等。
面上得很快。陆辞拿起筷子拌了拌，低头吃了一口，嚼了嚼，点头说了一句“不错“，就不再说话了，埋头吃得认真。
苏尘坐在对面，端着汤碗慢慢喝着，也不催他。
吃到一半，陆辞放下筷子，抬头看了苏尘一眼，忽然开口说了一句：
“你知道我来朔州是干什么的吗？“

苏尘端着汤碗的手没停，喝了一口，放下，才说：“买马。“
“买马是顺带的。“陆辞夹了一筷子面送进嘴里，嚼完咽下去，才继续说，“我主要不是来买马的。“
苏尘没接话，等着他说下去。
陆辞放下筷子，往椅背上一靠，目光落在街对面屋顶上几只正在啄食的麻雀身上，语气随意得像是在说别人的事：
“我来找个人。“
苏尘看了他一眼。
“找到了吗？“
“没有。“陆辞说，语气里没什么失落，更像是在陈述一个意料之中的结果，“本来也没抱太大希望。就是……家里有些旧事，跟这边的人有些关联，我爹让我顺路过来看看能不能找到点什么线索。“
“什么旧事？“
陆辞摇了摇头，嘴角带着一丝不太明显的苦笑：
“我也说不清楚。翻来覆去就那几句话——说这个人当年帮过家里很大的忙，后来因为一些变故分开了，再后来就断了联系。我爹只知道那个人最后出现在北边，具体在哪儿也说不准，让我沿路打听打听。“
他拿起桌上的粗瓷茶壶给自己倒了一碗水，喝了一口，皱了皱眉——大概是觉得这茶粗糙，比不上家里的，但还是咽了下去。
“从南边一路走上来，问了几个地方，都没什么线索。“他把茶碗放回桌上，手指在碗沿上轻轻叩了两下，“到朔州算是最后一站了。要是这儿也问不到，那就只能回去了。“
苏尘端起自己面前的汤碗，喝了一口，没有急着说话。
他在想一个问题——什么样的“旧事“，值得一个带着管家和护卫的少年从南方专程跑到北边来找人？以陆辞的穿着打扮和随行人员的规格，这个“家里“的规模和地位都不会小。能让这样的人家花这么多精力来找的人——要么是有恩于他们家，要么是握着他们家什么重要的东西。
但陆辞说话的语气不像是在撒谎，也不像是在刻意隐瞒什么重要信息。他说的“帮过家里很大的忙“这个说法，听起来确实像是真话。
“你要找的那个人，“苏尘问，“有什么特征？“
陆辞想了想，摇了摇头：
“我也没见过。我爹也只见过一面，说是个中年人，当时三十来岁的样子，身手很好，具体多好他也说不上来……就是说'一看就不是普通人'。除此之外就没有别的了。“

The next morning, Su Chen arrived at the big locust tree at Dongjiekou on time.
The late autumn sunshine was warmer than yesterday, shining a faint white light on the bluestone road. Most of the shops on the street were open, and there were vegetable sellers, cloth sellers, and breakfast sellers, and shouts came and went. The air is mixed with the smell of burnt bread and dew on green vegetables, which is what every ordinary morning in Shuozhou City should be like.
Su Chen stood under the locust tree for less than a moment when he saw Lu Ci coming from the corner of the street.
Today he changed into a pair of dark gray casual clothes with narrow sleeves. He still had the sapphire pendant hanging around his waist, but he lost a bit of the dazzling look of a rich young man from yesterday and looked more like a young man going out to do errands. The guard in gray followed him far behind. This time he kept a dozen steps away and did not get closer.
Lu Ci walked under the locust tree, glanced at Su Chen, smiled and said hello:
"Brother Su, good morning."
"Morning."
"Have you eaten?"
"Eat."
"I haven't eaten yet." Lu Ci said matter-of-factly, as if he didn't think there was anything wrong with being asked to wait for someone who had eaten breakfast. "I got up late in the morning. Uncle Chen urged me twice. I said I had an appointment with someone, but he didn't say it - let's go, you take me to find a place to fill my stomach first."
Su Chen glanced at him, turned around and walked into the street.
Lu Ci followed up with brisk steps and seemed to be in a good mood.
Su Chen took him to the noodle stall at the corner of East Street - the one he mentioned yesterday.
The noodle stall is not big, with two pots, one for cooking noodles and one for soup. The boss is an aunt in her fifties. Her apron is stained with flour, and her hands are very strong. She kneads the dough vigorously in her hands. Seeing Su Chen coming, he nodded as a greeting - Su Chen would come to this stall occasionally, so he wasn't a regular customer, but he recognized his face.
The two of them found a table to the side and sat down. Lu Ci ordered a bowl of mutton noodles with more chopped green onion, and two sesame seed cakes. Su Chen only had a bowl of clear soup and sat down to wait.
The face is very fast. Lu Ci picked up the chopsticks and mixed it, lowered his head and took a bite, chewed it, nodded and said "Not bad", stopped talking, and ate seriously.
Su Chen sat opposite, holding a bowl of soup and drinking slowly without urging him.
Halfway through eating, Lu Ci put down his chopsticks, looked up at Su Chen, and suddenly said:
"Do you know what I came to Shuozhou for?"
Su Chen kept holding the soup bowl, took a sip, put it down, and then said: "Buy a horse."
"Buying a horse is incidental." Lu Ci took a chopstick of noodles and put it into his mouth. After chewing and swallowing, he continued, "I'm not here mainly to buy a horse."
Su Chen didn't answer, waiting for him to continue.
Lu Ci put down his chopsticks and leaned back in his chair. His eyes fell on a few sparrows that were pecking at the roof across the street. His tone was casual, as if he was talking about someone else's business:
"I'm looking for someone."
Su Chen glanced at him.
"Did you find it?"
"No." Lu Ci said. There was no disappointment in his tone. It was more like stating an expected result. "I didn't have high hopes at first. It's just that... there are some old things at home that are related to people here. My dad asked me to stop by and see if I can find any clues."
"What old thing?"
Lu Ci shook his head, with a faint bitter smile on his lips:
"I can't tell clearly. I kept going over and over just a few words - saying that this person helped the family a lot back then, but later they separated due to some changes, and then lost contact. My father only knows that the person last appeared in the north, and he can't tell where exactly. He asked me to ask around along the way."
He picked up the rough porcelain teapot on the table and poured himself a bowl of water. He took a sip and frowned - probably because he thought the tea was rough and not as good as the one at home, but he still swallowed it.
"I walked all the way from the south and asked several places, but there were no clues." He put the tea bowl back on the table and put his fingers on the edge of the bowl.Knocking twice, he said, "It's our last stop to Shuozhou. If we can't ask here, we have no choice but to go back."
Su Chen picked up the soup bowl in front of him and took a sip without speaking in a hurry.
He was thinking about a question - what kind of "old things" are worthy of a young man with a butler and bodyguard traveling all the way from the south to the north to find someone? Judging from Lu Ci's dress and the size of his entourage, the size and status of this "family" are not small. The person who can make such a family spend so much energy to find someone - either he is kind to their family, or he holds something important to their family.
But Lu Ci's tone didn't sound like he was lying, nor did he sound like he was deliberately concealing any important information. What he said about "helping the family a lot" does sound like the truth.
"What are the characteristics of the person you are looking for?" Su Chen asked.
Lu Ci thought for a while and shook his head:
"I haven't seen him either. I've only seen my father once. He said he was a middle-aged man, in his thirties at the time, with very good skills. He couldn't tell how good he was... He just said, 'You can tell he's not an ordinary person at first sight.' There was nothing else."
